The dust here was different—finer, disturbed in long overlapping trails, as though thousands of feet had walked this exact path in a time that was not theirs. The compass in his pocket had stopped merely spinning; it was vibrating now, a frantic hum climbing up through his thigh and into his ribs.

text: Zik looked at the statue's blank face and understood, all at once, that the City had stopped testing them. If they forced the issue now they would spend the last of their strength against something that had never needed to fight them in the first place.

text: The statue waited another moment, as if confirming the decision, then turned and began to walk.

text: The corridor it led them down was narrower than the ones they had left, the ceiling lower, the air colder. The walls here carried no incomplete spirals. They carried names.
